meta.title: Korean — Stage C
meta.subtitle: 2,806 more words, taking you to about 5,791 — study after Stage B
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Korean → English (see the word in hangul, recall its meaning) and English → Korean. Each word is ONE note with TWO cards, each scheduled on its own. 2,806 words from stage C, the third and last of the three stages of the National Institute of the Korean Language's vocabulary list for learners (2003), taking you to about 5,791 words in all. TOPIK, the proficiency test, publishes no word list; this one is the state's own, graded by when a learner should meet each word. 48 of the stage's 2854 headwords are left out rather than glossed from nowhere: English Wiktionary has no entry for them, or none for the homograph the list means (만、인사、쓰이다 …) — mostly transparent derivatives such as -되다 and -적 forms of words carded here. The words are in the list's own order of frequency, commonest first. — The front shows the word in hangul; where the list has two words spelled alike (눈 "eye" and 눈 "snow"), it also shows the hanja or the phrase the list gives to tell them apart (203 of these). The back gives the Revised Romanization, the pronunciation in hangul where it differs from the spelling, the hanja of a Sino-Korean word, the meanings, a verb's or adjective's polite, past and formal forms, one row per hanja with its meaning, its eumhun and other words of the list written with it, and a fold of sentences. 1155 of the 2806 words carry example sentences, up to three apiece: real sentences from Tatoeba where the word has one meaning in the list, else the usage examples Wiktionary gives under the sense the card teaches, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside each. — Word list: 한국어 학습용 어휘 목록 (Korean vocabulary list for learners), National Institute of the Korean Language, 2003, under the Korea Open Government Licence Type 1. Meanings, romanization, pronunciation, hanja, conjugated forms and the examples marked as Wiktionary's: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Hanja meanings: the Unicode Unihan database (Unicode License). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, found with the Kiwi morphological analyser.
